_doc: Work notes on the site, newest first by date. Each: date, title, slug, summary, grade (measured, derived, borrowed or hypothetical, and where); the body is site/notes/<slug>.html.

notes.title: With the sideways pull held for the whole run, the shipped model keeps an offset that rises with the pull, about 3 m per m/s2 where the road stays in view; an outside estimate removes most of it (bench only)
notes.summary: Follow-up to the disturbance-estimate note, written after an outside review. The sideways pull is held for the whole 7.4 s run on the same 33 windows from 7 drives at two sizes (0.40 and 0.60 m/s2), with four arms: shipped; the outside estimate with its truck-model gain at 0.8; at 1.2; and at 0.8 one step (0.2 s) late. Runs that keep the road in view throughout, of 132: 41, 102, 121 and 103. On the 31 runs at the 0.40 pull valid in every arm, the median offset toward the pull at 3.2 s and 7.2 s is 0.86 and 1.24 m shipped; 0.43 and 0.52 with gain 0.8; 0.21 and 0.07 with gain 1.2; 0.44 and 0.52 late. Shipped is still creeping at the end (+0.11 m over the last 2 s) but flattening; at the 0.60 pull (9 valid runs) it ends at 1.55 m, and the paired ratio between the pulls is 1.34 against a pull ratio of 1.5. Sideways jerk is lower in every estimate arm (0.48 to 0.51 against 0.71). Undisturbed runs are 1.9 to 3.4 cm further from the recorded path in every estimate arm. 91 of 132 shipped runs leave the simulator's valid range, so the size over the whole set is not measured. The truck model in the estimate is the simulator's own with one number changed. Simulation only, not a change to the model, and no new mechanism.
notes.grade: Measured in simulation on the bench's truck model, two pull sizes, 33 windows from 7 drives, four arms. Readings written before the run. No sensor noise, road bank or tyre slip. The offsets come from the 31 and 9 runs that keep the road in view in every arm. Nothing run on a vehicle.
notes.result: offset toward a held pull at 7.2 s, 31 valid runs at 0.40: shipped 1.24 m, estimate gain 0.8 0.52, gain 1.2 0.07, one step late 0.52; about 3 m per m/s2 shipped; 91 of 132 shipped runs leave the valid range
notes.n: 33 windows, 7 drives; 132 runs per arm; 31 and 9 valid runs

notes.title: comma's own published bias test shows the failure our pull test found: a constant sideways push is not corrected, mostly at low speed
notes.summary: comma's public model report includes a "hugging" test: a constant sideways acceleration bias on a simulated car driven by the model. In the report we read, 22 of 96 runs pass, and the three largest misses shown are at 5 m/s (4.3 to 4.8 m off after about 5 s). Our bench pull test on a later model, measured the same way (against the model's own undisturbed run), finds the same weakness: 149 of 264 runs do not come back within 0.5 m, mostly under 10 m/s. A reading, not tested here: the policy's inputs include camera frames, intent and map channels but not its own earlier commands or measured sideways acceleration, so nothing in it accumulates a standing error. Qualified 2026-11-17 after an outside review: the model has a feature queue and recurrent state and could in principle learn to hold a correction, comma's simulated test names no lateral controller, and real cars running openpilot have an integral term below the model.
notes.grade: Borrowed (comma's public report, one model, read not rerun) next to measured (our bench pull test, simulation). The cause is a reading from the model's input list, not a test. Qualified 2026-11-17: the reading is not established.
notes.result: comma's hugging test 22 of 96 pass, largest misses at 5 m/s; our bench pull test 149 of 264 runs not back within 0.5 m, mostly under 10 m/s

notes.title: A sideways-pull estimate added outside the model cuts runs that do not come back: 85 to 27 of 132, but 16 to 2 of 44 where the road stays in view (bench only, corrected 2026-11-17)
notes.summary: Planned before the run, corrected after an outside review. An estimate of the outside sideways pull (measured sideways acceleration minus what a truck model predicts for the steering applied, smoothed over half a second) is subtracted from the model's steering request; the model is unchanged. Two pull sizes (0.40 and 0.60 m/s2) on 33 windows from 7 drives, 132 runs: runs that do not come back within 0.5 m, measured after the pull has ended, fall from 85 to 14 with an exact truck model and to 27 with its steering gain 20% wrong. The review found that the count is taken after the pull ends, so it measures a slow or lost return and not a standing offset; that the simulator lost its view of the road on 68 of the 132 shipped runs (64 keep view throughout, against 114 with the estimate); that on the 44 runs at the 0.40 pull valid in both, shipped ends 0.89 m off at the end of the pull and 0.35 m four seconds later, with 16 not back against 2; and that the estimate's truck model is the simulator's own with one number changed. The claim that the result confirms the missing-state explanation is withdrawn. The rule named four pull sizes and two were run, so it was not run as written. No new mechanism: this is textbook control. A test that holds the pull for the whole run is in its own note.
notes.grade: Measured in simulation on the bench's truck model, two pull sizes and one smoothing time. Pull injected as the quantity the estimate measures; no sensor noise, delay, road bank or tyre slip. Nothing run on a vehicle. Corrected 2026-11-17 after outside review; the size over all 132 runs is inflated by lost road view.
notes.result: runs not back within 0.5 m, 132 runs, measured after the pull ends: 85 shipped, 14 exact truck model, 27 gain 20% wrong; on 44 runs valid in both (0.40 pull) 16 shipped against 2; explanation claim withdrawn; rule not run as written
notes.n: 33 windows, 7 drives, 2 pull sizes; 44 runs valid in both arms; 8 turn windows, 4 drives

notes.title: The turn signal does not help the plan speed, through the model's intent input or as a small learned offset
notes.summary: After a turn signal comes on the driver slows by 1.4 to 2.1 m/s over 4 to 8 s at 9 m/s and over, and the model, which does not see the signal, plans 0.5 to 1.2 m/s too fast. Two quick looks asked whether the signal can fix the plan speed. Fed through the intent input (103 onsets on 15 drives), the plan error changes by -0.05 m/s at 6 s [-0.11, +0.01] and -0.08 m/s at 8 s [-0.17, -0.04], against an error of about 2 m/s. As a least-squares offset while the signal is on, fitted leaving each drive out, the error gets worse: +0.12 m/s at 4 s, +0.23 at 6 s, +0.33 at 8 s, with intervals including zero. Both dropped. These are validation drives that had been looked at before, so this is not a held-out test.
notes.grade: Measured open loop on the 17 validation drives of one truck and one driver, existing captures of the shipped model, on drives that had been looked at before (a design-set look, not held out). No training, no new model runs, no simulator, nothing deployed. A negative result.
notes.result: intent input: plan speed error -0.05 m/s at 6 s [-0.11, +0.01] against about 2 m/s; learned offset: worse, +0.12 m/s at 4 s, +0.23 at 6 s, +0.33 at 8 s; both dropped

notes.title: Averaging the plan with the plan from a mirrored scene is not closer to the driver (-0.002 m at 4 s); the two plans disagree by 0.20 m
notes.summary: Planned before the run. Mirror the camera picture and the traffic-side input, run comma's model, mirror its sideways plan back, and compare with the normal plan. Open loop on 6 drives (39,520 steps), stock model. Averaging the two plans changes the sideways error against the driver at 4 s from 0.381 m to 0.378 m (-0.002 m [-0.007, +0.002]), so the idea is killed by its pre-set rule. The two plans differ by 0.20 m on average at 4 s; the signed part is 0.06 m to the left [-0.11, -0.01], and the mirrored scene is planned 0.29 m/s slower. A mirrored scene is left-hand traffic and puts the off-centre camera on the other side, so this does not separate a model bias from the scene or the camera position.
notes.grade: Measured open loop on 6 drives of one truck and one driver with the current camera position, real frames, stock model with no adapter. Test and kill rule written before the run. No training, no simulator, nothing deployed. A negative result; the 0.20 m disagreement and 0.06 m signed part are descriptions, with the scene and the camera position not separated from the model.
notes.result: averaged plan 0.378 m against 0.381 m normal at 4 s (-0.002 m [-0.007, +0.002]); plans disagree by 0.20 m at 4 s, signed part 0.06 m [-0.11, -0.01]; mirrored scene planned 0.29 m/s slower; killed

notes.title: Combining overlapping speed plans is worse than a plain low-pass filter at the same smoothness (+0.049 m/s² for two plans)
notes.summary: Each step the model plans speed, so several earlier plans also predicted the same moment. Combining them, as in robot action chunking, might smooth the command without a filter's lag. The test named by the idea's own source: at matched smoothness, is it better than a one-pole low-pass filter on the newest plan? Open loop on the 6 of 17 validation drives with enough unbroken history (7,193 steps), no training. Every combined arm is worse than the filter on all 6 drives: two plans +0.049 m/s² [+0.030, +0.076] in tracking error, three plans +0.158, their median +0.094. Older plans are worse predictions of the same moment, not independent ones. Killed; not run on held-out drives.
notes.grade: Measured open loop on 6 drives of one truck and one driver, existing capture of the shipped model, on validation drives that had been looked at before (a design-set look, not held out). The command is read from the plan, not the action output the truck uses. No training, no simulator, nothing deployed. A negative result.
notes.result: two plans +0.049 m/s² [+0.030, +0.076] worse than a low-pass filter at the same jerk, three plans +0.158, median +0.094; worse on all 6 drives; killed

notes.title: A sideways direction in the model's map-feature input: one weak, consistent direction on 17 drives, worth roughly 10 to 25 cm at 4 s by extrapolation
notes.summary: Planned before the run. The driving model takes a 64-number map-feature input. Is there one fixed direction in it that moves the plan sideways the same way on different roads? A sensitivity probe, open loop on real frames of 17 drives (493 probes, map input zero as on the truck): the effect of a small change along the common direction on the 4 s sideways plan has the same sign in 97% of probes (98% at 2 s, 100% for the steering command), the leave-one-drive-out cosine with the other drives' direction is 0.37, and the direction has no effect on plan speed. The effect is weak: 0.3 cm per unit of the scale fixed in advance, and roughly 10 to 25 cm at 4 s over the range real map features occupy, by extrapolating a local slope, which is not a measurement. Parked: a controller writing this input would need information the model cannot already see, and none was found.
notes.grade: Measured open loop on real camera frames of 17 drives of one truck and one driver, 493 probes, central differences on the model's own inputs, one adapter. The size over the real map range is an extrapolation of a local slope and is derived, not measured. Test and rule written before the run. No training, no simulator, nothing deployed.
notes.result: same sign in 97% of 493 probes, leave-one-drive-out cosine 0.37, no effect on speed; about 0.3 cm per planned unit, roughly 10 to 25 cm at 4 s over the real map range by extrapolation; weak, parked

notes.title: How the truck feeds comma's model against comma's own reference: one input was always zero, and the traffic-side setting is the right one (+0.004 m at 4 s if changed)
notes.summary: After the turn-signal gap was found, every model input and processing step the truck uses was compared by reading with the copy of comma's reference code and notes. Same as the reference: the pulse rule for the intent input, the image warp and focal lengths, which camera feeds which input, the 20 Hz pacing and in-graph history, the smoothing of the speed command, and the reset on a non-finite output. Different: the intent input was zeros (see the turn-signal note). Two comments in the truck's code disagreed on what the traffic-side setting means, so it was measured: on 17 drives, feeding the other setting changes the plan's sideways error at 4 s from 0.352 to 0.356 m (+0.004 m, by-drive interval [+0.000, +0.009]), with 14 of 17 drives slightly worse. The truck feeds the right one, and the input barely matters to this model. Four further differences are in live timing and image handling and were not measured.
notes.grade: The comparison is by reading code, not measured. The traffic-side input is measured open loop on real camera frames of 17 drives of one truck and one driver, the setting fed now against the other, with the run unchanged otherwise. No training, no simulator, nothing deployed.
notes.result: plan error at 4 s 0.352 m as fed, 0.356 m with the other traffic-side setting (+0.004 m [+0.000, +0.009], 14 of 17 drives worse); no other difference found that changes the plan on recorded drives

notes.title: Feeding the turn signal to the model's intent input: the plan follows lane changes more closely on 17 drives, not confirmed on two other sets
notes.summary: Planned before the run, tested twice more. The driving model has an input for the driver's stated intent, and the truck's stack has always fed it zeros. Open loop on real frames, one pulse at each recorded turn-signal onset, scored as the sideways gap between the planned path and the driver's path at 4 s ahead. On 17 held-out drives (134 onsets) the gap after a signal falls from 1.22 to 0.88 m (-28%, 95% by drive [-0.47, -0.19] m). On a second set of six drives (37 onsets) it falls 12% with an interval that includes zero. A third test, written in advance to the reviewers' specification (stock model, one lane-change pulse at an onset at 9 m/s and over, 47 events on 14 other drives), gives a plan change of -0.22 m with a by-drive interval of [-0.32, +0.11] m (-0.06 [-0.23, +0.19] without the largest drive), which includes zero, so its rule fails. The steering command's error against the driver fell by 0.11 to 0.12 m/s2 at three lags, with intervals excluding zero, and that is recorded as a lead only. It improves one lane-change-heavy drive (one drive holds 24 of the 47 events; the mean of the 14 per-drive means is -0.04 m); on the other drives it is indistinguishable from zero, with one large overshoot on a turn. The 14 drives are about 9 or 10 trips, so by-drive intervals are too narrow. It is an input used as intended, not an improvement to the model, and it is parked.
notes.grade: Measured open loop on real camera frames of one truck and one driver: 17 held-out drives (134 signal onsets), a second set of 6 drives (37 onsets), and a third set of 14 drives with events from 17 captured (47 onsets, stock model, never read for this question). Tests and pass rules written before each run. No training, no simulator, nothing deployed. Neither later set meets the rule; the scoring window and pulse placement have known limits.
notes.result: gap to the driver's path at 4 s after a signal onset: 1.22 to 0.88 m (-28%) on 17 drives; 1.23 to 1.08 m (-12%, interval includes zero) on 6 other drives; plan change -0.22 m, by-drive interval [-0.32, +0.11] on 47 events from 14 more drives, so the planned rule fails; it improves one lane-change-heavy drive and is indistinguishable from zero on the others, with one large overshoot on a turn; parked
notes.n: 17 drives, 134 onsets; 6 drives, 37 onsets; 14 drives, 47 events

notes.title: No line-type offset in the plan: on roads with a centre line and no painted right line, comma's plan sits where the driver drove (-0.002 m at 4 s)
notes.summary: Planned before the result was read. Open loop on 17 held-out drives (real frames, no simulator): on two-way roads where the model sees a centre line and no painted right line, does its planned path sit to one side of where the driver drove? Straight driving only, 50,570 steps, road class from the model's own line confidences. For the truck's adapter at 4 s ahead the offset is -0.022 m [-0.053, +0.053] with both lines and -0.002 m [-0.042, +0.039] with a centre line only; paired by drive the difference is 0.000 m [-0.055, +0.064]. The pass rule (10 cm, interval excluding zero) is not met, so this is closed: no line-type offset in the plan. The reference is where this driver drove, not the lane centre.
notes.grade: Measured open loop on 17 held-out drives of one truck and one driver, real camera frames, 50,570 straight-driving steps. Test and pass rule written before the result was read. No training, no simulator, nothing deployed. A negative result.
notes.result: centre-line-only offset -0.002 m [-0.042, +0.039] at 4 s against -0.022 m [-0.053, +0.053] with both lines; paired difference 0.000 m [-0.055, +0.064]; the 10 cm rule is not met, closed
notes.n: 17 drives, 50,570 straight-driving steps (5,566 on 15 drives with a centre line only)

notes.title: Training the correction head: most of the measured effect was the untrained start with a doubled bound, not the teacher. Corrected result, closed after a test on new drives
notes.summary: Corrected and extended 2026-11-16, closed the same day. Only the learned correction of comma's policy was trained, in closed loop in the simulator on 73 windows from four recorded drives of one truck and one driver, by imitation of a teacher, and scored on 30 validation windows from 6 other drives (120 pushed episodes per push type). Every retrained head started from the correction with its bound doubled and was compared with the shipped model, whose bound is normal. That untrained start, with zero training, already gives most of the measured effect on a sideways step: distance at 4 s -0.133 m [-0.174, -0.094] against shipped, set by 2 s and flat after, with a smaller and smoother command and no change in ordinary driving. Reviewers attribute it to the bench's sideways step: right after it the frozen base policy turns the wrong way for about a second, and a larger bound cancels more of that. It is a head start made by the bench, not a faster return. Against that untrained start the teacher adds 8 to 12 cm at 4 s on the step and 15 to 19 cm on the yaw push at quarter and half gain, while the bench's own verdicts (recovered share) stay flat, with an overshoot on the yaw push and, in three of four runs below full gain, about 10 cm of extra width in ordinary turns that comes from the training. Controls kept: a gain sweep, the teacher run as the controller with no learning (the overshoot is the teacher's; the heading term is needed), a zero-gain training run, and commanded jerk (full gain is harsher than shipped). Earlier claims that the lead survives a no-training comparator and that the trained head recovers like the privileged controller are withdrawn. Test one (teacher steering toward the driver's path) was negative. Update 2026-11-16: on a push that builds up over 3.2 s with no sideways jump (seven fixed models, run once), the doubled limit alone is 3 to 4 cm from shipped, and against the untrained start the teacher's effect is ordered by strength, absent at zero strength at 4 s, and repeats on a second seed (half gain at 4 s: -0.159 m [-0.186, -0.129] and -0.181 m [-0.209, -0.152]). An outside review reads this as smaller displacement while the push is running, not a faster return: lane contact restates it, the recovered verdict is at a ceiling set by the unpushed runs, and peak commanded jerk rises 32 to 42% at half gain. The teacher run as the controller with no learning gives the same reduction, so the trained head copies it from the camera with lower average commanded jerk and the same peak. Closed 2026-11-16 after a test written down before it was run, on 38 windows from 11 drives never used in this work: against the untrained start the trained heads are about 20 cm lower at the peak of the slow push and about 12 cm closer afterwards, and reading the unchanged model's plan 0.5 s further ahead with no training gets about 17 cm and 9 cm. The heads' remaining 3 to 5 cm is not separable from zero on 11 drives, they are rougher under the push, and each had one ordinary window past the contact line. One of three conditions set in advance was met, and two outside reviews agreed to close. A real effect in the bench, not an improvement over a one-number setting.
notes.grade: Measured in simulation on recorded G55 drives: 30 validation windows from 6 drives of one truck and one driver, 120 pushed episodes per push type, test one one seed, test two three seeds at full gain, two at half gain, one each at quarter and zero gain, plus an untrained start; nothing deployed. A corrected, negative and parked result: three outside reviews and a control run overturned the first reading.
notes.result: the untrained start with a doubled bound gives -0.133 m at 4 s on a sideways step against shipped with no training, but only 3 to 4 cm on a push with no jump; against that start the teacher adds 8 to 12 cm on the step, 15 to 19 cm on the yaw push and 7 to 26 cm on the slow push (ordered by strength), which reads as smaller displacement during the push, with peak commanded jerk up 32 to 42% at half gain and no change in the bench's recovered verdicts; closed after a planned test on new drives: about 20 cm lower at the peak of the slow push than its untrained start, against about 17 cm for a longer delay request with no training, and rougher under the push; not a method
notes.n: 30 windows, 120 pushed episodes per push type, 6 drives; 8 trained runs plus an untrained start

notes.title: Camera adapter variants in turns, closed loop: the shipped adapter tracks the driver's path as well as the stock model, and the variant trained without driver labels runs about 15 cm wider
notes.summary: Closed-loop push bench (simulated vehicle, 30 validation windows from 6 recorded drives of one truck and one driver), turn measure: offset to the outside of the driver's recorded path on the steps where the shipped adapter's unpushed run commands 0.7 m/s2 or more (9 windows). Shipped adapter 0.199 m; stock model 0.231 m (+0.031 m [-0.046, +0.100] against shipped, 2 of 9 windows further inside); lane paint + teacher variant, trained without the driver's path labels, 0.345 m (+0.146 m [+0.109, +0.184], 0 of 9 windows further inside). The shipped adapter does not run wider than stock in turns. The variant with the highest open-loop turn gain runs widest, so open-loop turn gain did not predict closed-loop turn tracking. Distance from the path on straight steps is 0.170, 0.171 and 0.171 m. Nine windows from three drives, one seed, the driver's path as the reference; two more variants were added later the same day (lane paint + teacher + pose 0.275 m, +0.075 m [+0.057, +0.095], 0 of 9; shipped recipe at 16 epochs 0.213 m, +0.014 m [-0.026, +0.059], 3 of 9, with push displacement at 2 s +0.024 m [+0.015, +0.032]). Order in turns: shipped, 16 epochs, stock, pose, no driver labels. Driver path labels are the term that matters for this measure, pose labels recover about half of the gap, and four times the training on the same drives adds nothing in turns. No outside review: nothing is claimed beyond confirming the shipped adapter.
notes.grade: Measured in simulation on recorded G55 drives: 30 validation windows from 6 drives of one truck and one driver (9 carry the turn result, from 3 drives), one seed, per-step traces, nothing deployed. No outside review.
notes.result: in turns the shipped adapter sits 0.199 m outside the driver's path, stock 0.231 m (difference +0.031 m [-0.046, +0.100]), the variant without driver labels 0.345 m (+0.146 m [+0.109, +0.184], wider on all 9 windows)

notes.title: Push bench by which lane lines the road has: on centre-line-only roads a push to the right ends half a metre past the unpushed path at 4 s
notes.summary: The closed-loop push bench's 30 validation windows (simulated vehicle, 6 drives of one truck and one driver) split by which lane lines the model sees in the unpushed run: 17 with a line on both sides, 12 with a centre line only (two-way roads with a double yellow line and a curb), 1 with neither. Medians over episodes, pushed minus unpushed, 1.0 m push: to the left, 0.05 m (both) and 0.02 m (centre only) at 4 s; to the right, -0.26 m (both) and -0.53 m (centre only) at 4 s, -0.10 and -0.18 m at 5.6 s. A push to the right displaces the truck less while applied (0.34 to 0.37 m against 0.52 to 0.60 m) and is followed by a swing past the unpushed run to the left, about a quarter of a metre with both lines and about half a metre with the centre line only. These are medians, not the tail; road type is confounded with speed and curvature; 12 and 17 windows, one seed; the class comes from the model's own confidences; the model's line distance is not a position measurement; the asymmetry may come from the bench. No outside review, because nothing is claimed. A recovery share from this bench mixes road types and push directions that behave differently, so it should be reported apart.
notes.grade: Measured in simulation on recorded G55 drives: 30 validation windows from 6 drives of one truck and one driver (17 and 12 in the two classes tabulated), one seed, no training, nothing deployed. A description of the bench; no outside review.
notes.result: 1.0 m push to the left is back within 5 cm by 4 s on both road types; a push to the right swings past the unpushed run to the left: -0.26 m (both lines) and -0.53 m (centre line only) at 4 s, -0.10 and -0.18 m at 5.6 s
notes.n: 30 windows (17 both lines, 12 centre line only, 1 neither); 17 or 12 episodes per cell

notes.title: The policy's steering responds to its lateral delay request: a larger request takes less displacement from a push and puts the truck further to the outside of turns, a smaller one the reverse; no setting is better on everything
notes.summary: comma's policy takes an input for how much steering delay it should compensate; the truck adapter feeds 0.275 s. Closed-loop push bench, simulated vehicle, 25 validation windows at 10 m/s and over (100 pushed episodes), request set to 0.275, 0.375, 0.475 and 0.775 s, paired by episode to 0.275 s. The displacement peak within the push is smaller in 50 of 50 episodes at every larger request: 1.0 m push -0.034 m [-0.038, -0.030] at 0.375 s, -0.068 [-0.079, -0.059] at 0.475 s, -0.129 [-0.153, -0.111] at 0.775 s; 1.5 m push -0.071, -0.136, -0.227 m. Overshoot (1.0 m) -0.031 [-0.046, -0.018], -0.066, -0.102 m. By 5.6 s no difference (+0.003 m [-0.015, +0.019] at 0.375 s). Unpushed steering activity rises with the request. This is a sensitivity result, not a better setting: the effect grows steadily with no best value, and the bench's controller already compensates the simulated vehicle's lag. The first reading, a matched value with a larger gain, was wrong: the larger number came from taking the peak over the whole episode and from the slow windows, and two outside model reviews caught it. Addendum: three settings below the current one were run (0.175, 0.075, 0.0 s), seven in all. In turns (9 windows) the truck sits further to the outside of the driver's path as the request grows: 0.199 m at 0.275 s, 0.246 at 0.375 s, 0.365 at 0.775 s, and 0.159, 0.122 and 0.083 m at 0.175, 0.075 and 0.0 s; push displacement at 2 s moves the other way (0.633 m at 0.275 s, 0.424 at 0.775 s, 0.685 at 0.0 s). The request trades push displacement against position in turns in both directions; no setting is better on everything. Second addendum: the request was given separately to the policy's base part and to its learned correction in two crossed runs. Base at 0.775 s with the correction at 0.275 s: push displacement at 2 s -0.356 m [-0.395, -0.323] and turn offset +0.204 m [+0.108, +0.304] against 0.275 s (both at 0.775 s: -0.210 and +0.166 m). Correction at 0.775 s with the base at 0.275 s: +0.580 m and -0.117 m. Both effects follow the base part's request and the correction's request works against them; neither crossed setting is better on both measures, and a crossed request is an input the policy was never trained on. One seed, simulated vehicle; the vehicle has no steering actuator, so nothing changes on the road.
notes.grade: Measured in simulation on recorded G55 drives: 25 validation windows at 10 m/s and over (from the 30 validation windows of 6 drives of one truck and one driver), one seed, no training, nothing deployed. Two outside-model reviews changed the reading.
notes.result: each extra 0.1 s of lateral request takes about 3 cm (1.0 m push) to 7 cm (1.5 m push) off the displacement within the push (-0.034 m [-0.038, -0.030] at 0.375 s, 1.0 m); no difference by 5.6 s; in turns the truck sits about 4 to 5 cm further to the outside per 0.1 s, and smaller requests reverse both; seven settings, none better on everything
notes.n: 25 windows at 10 m/s and over, 100 pushed episodes

notes.title: Inside comma's policy: the learned correction opposes an imposed turn at every speed, and on real low-speed turns the full policy asks 6 to 9% less than the driver took
notes.summary: comma's policy output is a base action plus a learned correction. Splitting the exported model gives the two parts at each step. Push bench (simulated vehicle, 30 validation windows): during the imposed turn the correction opposes it at every speed (93 to 100% of steps); above 10 m/s the base does not respond; under 10 m/s (5 windows) the base steers with the turn by 1.2 to 2.2 m/s2, more than the correction's bound of 1, so the whole policy follows it. At low speed such a swing looks like the start of a turn, so this may be reasonable for a policy with no route. Real driving, open loop, 17 held-out drives, per turn event at 5 to 10 m/s: full action / driver 0.939 [0.872, 1.014] (stock) and 0.914 [0.865, 0.967] (adapter), base / driver 0.999 [0.959, 1.052] and 0.985 [0.956, 1.023]; the difference excludes zero by drive. The first per-step table (83% against 93% in tight turns) selected on the driver's outcome and overstated this; controls on lag and on binning by the base's own request agree. This describes how the two parts divide the work; it is modest, not an improvement and not evidence the correction is wrong. The base alone does not drive in closed loop, nothing here measures running wide, steps under 5 m/s are not in the data, and no route was fed. Two outside model reviews criticised the first reading, and part of the open-loop picture was already known from earlier work in this project. Update 2026-11-17, speed half, open loop on the same 17 drives (about 72,700 steps): the full action tracks the driver's acceleration slightly better than the base alone (correlation 0.777 against 0.715; mean absolute error 0.200 against 0.215 m/s2, by-drive difference -0.025 to -0.005). The base changes about 2.5 times more from step to step (0.34 against 0.14 m/s2 per 0.2 s), so the correction mostly smooths it. In steps where the driver braked or accelerated harder than 1 m/s2 the full action asks for less than the driver did; those bands are selected by the driver's outcome. A description, no test follows.
notes.grade: Measured: push bench in simulation (30 validation windows, 5 under 10 m/s) and open loop on 17 held-out drives of one truck and one driver. No training, no closed-loop comparison, nothing deployed. Two outside-model reviews changed the reading.
notes.result: correction opposes an imposed turn at every speed; at 5 to 10 m/s the full policy asks 6 to 9% less than the driver took per turn event (0.939 [0.872, 1.014] stock), the base asks the same (0.999 [0.959, 1.052])
notes.n: 30 bench windows (5 under 10 m/s); 17 drives, 69 turn events at 5 to 10 m/s

notes.title: Raising the steering correction's bound cancels more of a sideways push while it is applied, but returns to the path no faster; closed after a sustained-pull test
notes.summary: Closed-loop bench, simulated vehicle, 30 validation windows from 6 drives, a yaw push of 1.0 or 1.5 m applied over the first 2 s. Editing comma's exported model so the steering correction's tanh bound is 2 or 3 instead of 1 (no training) cancels more of the push while it is applied: against the shipped adapter, distance from path at push end -0.186 m [-0.254, -0.125] (bound 2) and -0.242 m [-0.339, -0.155] (bound 3), departures -5.8 and -7.5 points, lane error -0.248 and -0.271 m. The recovered share does not move (+1.7 points [-2.5, +6.7]). The steering half carries all of it; the speed half only adds unpushed speed error. The correction is above 0.8 of its bound in a fifth to two fifths of push steps and in 0.0 to 0.1% of unpushed steps. When every arm drives at bound 1 through the push and switches at push end, all start from the same offset (0.844 m) and the raised bound returns no faster (distance at 4 s -0.010 m [-0.037, +0.010]; recovered share 1.7 points lower). The first reading, that the raised bound recovers sooner, was wrong: two outside model reviews pointed out that the push is applied while the policy steers. Update 2026-11-17, closed after a planned test: a constant sideways pull inside the simulated vehicle for 3.2 s at four sizes (0.30 to 0.60 m/s2), 33 low-speed windows from 7 drives (264 pulled episodes per model), scored once. With the steering correction written as 2*tanh(x/2), no training, 129 of 264 runs end more than 0.5 m from the model's own undisturbed run against 149 with the shipped file (by-drive 95% interval of the share difference [-0.131, -0.025]); at 1.0 m, 76 against 108. Largest distance under the pull is lower in 33 of 33 windows, and undisturbed driving is unchanged. Closed by a stop rule: in only 10 of 27 rescued runs was the shipped correction at its limit during the pull (half needed); the gain is less compression near the limit. In the bench's other map mode the interval includes zero, and the rescued runs are partly ones that left the rendered view. Two outside reviews agreed to close.
notes.grade: Measured in simulation on recorded G55 drives: 30 validation windows from 6 drives, one model file edited per arm, no training, the bench's vehicle model has no tyre or roll limit. Two outside-model reviews changed the reading; nothing deployed. Update 2026-11-17: 33 windows from 7 drives, simulated vehicle with a yaw-rate pull and no sideslip; planned before the run, scored once, two outside reviews.
notes.result: raised bound cancels more of the push while applied (distance at push end -0.186 m [-0.254, -0.125] at bound 2); from an equal offset it returns no faster (-0.010 m [-0.037, +0.010] at 4 s); closed again 2026-11-17 after a planned test with a sustained pull: 129 against 149 of 264 runs end more than 0.5 m from the undisturbed run, no undisturbed cost, but the shipped correction was at its limit in only 10 of 27 rescued runs; a bench effect, not a method
notes.n: 30 windows, 6 drives, 120 pushed episodes per arm; update: 33 windows, 7 drives, 264 pulled episodes per model

notes.title: Given the route on its map input, the frozen model slows a little more before turns, but a corridor that stops at the junction does as much
notes.summary: Open loop on one truck and one driver, no training: the frozen model (as it runs on the truck) rolled out under five navigation map inputs (zeros, roads, a corridor along the current road that stops at the first junction, the driven route, and the route mirrored) on 8 drives, 37,362 steps. At 8 s the route lowers planned-speed error on turn approaches by 0.70 m/s (-1.03 to -0.38, 8 of 8 drives), against 3.53 with zeros. Before braking starts (229 steps) the corridor that stops at the junction does as much (-0.66) as the route (-0.64) and the mirrored route (-0.66), so the effect is not route-specific; the route separates only where the driver is already braking. Part of every gain is that the baseline plan is already 0.5 m/s fast. The first reading, that a route helps anticipation, did not survive two outside reviews. Not run: straight-through and wrong-turn corridors, timing shifts, a corridor-width sweep, a zeros-map adapter baseline. No adapter trained; the branch is parked.
notes.grade: Measured open loop on recorded drives of one truck and one driver: 8 drives, 46,844 steps (37,362 with a valid route and speed of 2 m/s or more); the not-yet-braking cells are 229 and 106 steps. No training, no closed-loop run. Two outside-model reviews changed the reading; nothing deployed.
notes.result: route turn approaches: 8 s error 3.53 m/s with zeros, -0.70 with the route; before braking the stopping corridor does as much (-0.66 against -0.64), so not route-specific
notes.n: 8 drives, 37,362 steps; 229 steps before braking starts

notes.title: The stock model's planned speed is 2 to 4 m/s fast before route turns the driver has not begun braking for
notes.summary: Open loop on one truck and one driver, no training: three checks on the stock model's planned speed. (1) The earlier metric included the model's error in reading current speed (0.75 m/s on stock). Anchored to measured speed, the 8 s error is 1.331 m/s for stock and 1.293 for the shipped adapter, against 1.823 for holding speed, so the adapter's planned-speed gain is mostly a better reading of current speed. This corrects the route-memory note: the remembered-speed blend lowers 8 s error on repeated road from 1.73 to 1.48 m/s (-0.24 [-0.39, -0.09], 11 of 13 drives), not 1.83 to 1.52. (2) In the step average a route has little room: route turns are 3.2% of steps and about 7% of absolute error, and above 22 m/s the plan is no better than holding speed (per-drive difference +0.006 [-0.124, +0.111] m/s). (3) Per event, before a route turn the driver has not begun braking for, the plan slows about half as much as the driver and is 2 to 4 m/s fast at 8 s (412 steps, 9 drives). Not shown: whether the turns were optional or forced, and the effect of lead vehicles. Next: feed the frozen stock model the planned route and see whether it plans more of the slowing.
notes.grade: Measured open loop on recorded drives of one truck and one driver: 23 drives, 114,375 steps (19 validation drives, 84,869 steps; map context on 10 drives, 60,526 steps). No training, no closed-loop run. Two outside-model reviews changed check 3; nothing deployed.
notes.result: anchored 8 s planned-speed error 1.331 m/s (stock); plan is 2 to 4 m/s fast before route turns the driver has not begun braking for
notes.n: 23 drives, 114,375 steps; 412 steps on 9 drives for the turn approaches

notes.title: In closed loop no adapter variant separates from the shipped adapter, and stock is 4 points behind it
notes.summary: Closed loop in the simulator on one truck and one driver: five arms (the shipped rig adapter, two lane-paint-plus-teacher variants without driver labels, an all-terms 2-minute variant, and stock with no adapter) on 30 held-out windows from 6 sessions, each run unpushed and pushed 1.0 and 1.5 m (120 pushed episodes per arm). Pushed recovery is 0.492 for shipped and 0.475 to 0.483 for the variants, with intervals about 6 points wide, so no variant separates from shipped and a loss of up to about 7 points is not excluded. Stock recovers 0.450, 4 points behind. Relative recovery is identical across arms on shared episodes, so these windows cannot separate models this close, and the recipe differences are not read as effects. One seed per arm; the adapter line is closed for the general goal.
notes.grade: Measured in simulation on recorded G55 drives: 30 held-out windows from 6 sessions, one training seed per arm, no per-episode rows saved, session intervals use 6 clusters. Two outside-model reviews; nothing deployed to the truck.
notes.result: no variant separates from shipped (recovered 0.475 to 0.483 against 0.492); stock 0.450

notes.title: Remembering a road helps planned speed, but it is route memory
notes.summary: Open loop on one truck and one driver. The rig adapter's gain is not memory of its training roads: adapted minus stock lateral plan error at 4 s is -0.017 m on roads over 200 m from the training drives, and the time-zero speed-scale gain holds on 17 of 17 drives there. Training 16 epochs instead of 4 did not improve the plan on trained roads. Plan error repeats weakly by place (correlation 0.29 against 0.06 for a shifted control). Blending the speed the driver held at the same place on earlier drives into stock's planned speed lowers 8 s speed error from 1.83 to 1.52 m/s on 11 of 13 drives. This is route memory: it helps only on road already driven, and it is not an improvement to the driving model. Two outside model reviews agreed. No model was trained on it and the branch is parked.
notes.grade: Measured open loop on recorded drives of one truck and one driver (17 drives for the adapter split, 13 for the speed blend), no closed-loop run; the wrong-place control is weak because it changes road type. Two outside-model reviews; nothing trained or deployed.
notes.result: remembered speed lowers 8 s planned speed error 1.83 to 1.52 m/s; route memory, not a model improvement

notes.title: The rig adapter's lane fix is mostly geometry; its plan and speed gains need the driver's labels, and two minutes of data over-trains
notes.summary: A measured account of the adapter recipe: 27 training runs and 3 stock scorings, open loop on 17 validation drives, mostly one seed. Stock fed the teacher's warp and shifted by the 0.239 m camera offset reaches right lane 0.042 m and left 0.086 m from paint (shipped adapter 0.034 m, 0.039 m), but its 4 s plan error is 0.420 m. Lane paint plus teacher with no driver labels matches the shipped lane result (0.034 m, 0.040 m). The shipped plan (0.352 m against stock 0.376 m) and speed (2.1% against 3.6%) gains need the path and speed labels, which also lower turn gain (0.829 against 0.853). Two minutes of one stretch over-trained at 63 epochs (plan 0.468 m, speed 8.1%) and did not at 6 epochs (0.378 m, 2.9%). No variant beats the shipped adapter except on turn gain. The lane truth is the same paint detector that made the training labels.
notes.grade: Measured open loop on 17 validation drives of recorded G55 drives, mostly one seed, no closed-loop run; lane truth is the same classical paint detector that made the training labels, scored on straight, clearly painted frames at 8 to 12 m. Two outside-model reviews; nothing deployed to the truck.
notes.result: no variant beats the shipped adapter; lane 0.034 / 0.039 m, plan 0.352 m, speed 2.1%

notes.title: Removing CPU warps, cold graph loads and single-GPU limits speeds training and simulation 2.6x to 107x
notes.summary: Measured before and after on two 230 W 24 GB GPUs with NVLink and 64 CPU cores: memory-mapped graph caching cut model load from 21.22 s to 1.24 s in FP32 (17.1x, 0.0 diff) and 19.12 s to 1.15 s in BF16 (16.7x); batched vmap in bfloat16 with float32 adapter weights cut a 4-epoch full-corpus adapter run from 3.41 h to 1.26 h (2.7x) within 1.6 mm on all 4,552 validation paint frames, and scaled to 200.3 samples/s across 2 GPUs with NVLink DDP (1.98x vs 1-GPU B=64 accumulation, 0.0 step-1 gradient diff); CUDA splatting, pull-push hole fill and grid_sample warps (cuda_fast) cut render time from 172.2 ms to 5.64 ms/view (30.6x) and 60-episode rollouts to 29.9 s across 2 GPUs (5.9x, matching aggregate recovery while diverging earlier than the CPU reference at trajectory level, onset p = 0.00098); and memory-mapped 5 Hz drive packs cut random-access ORT jump-ins from 1,385 ms to 13.0 ms (106.6x, 0.0 diff after a 149.2 s one-time pack build).
notes.grade: Measured on recorded G55 drives and dense closed-loop simulation windows with NVML hardware counters, gradient parity checks and trajectory-equivalence checks (cuda_fast fails step-by-step onset, p = 0.00098); CPU reference simulator unchanged.
notes.result: 2.7x 4-epoch train, 5.9x sim rollout, 106.6x jump-in
notes.n: 31,555 refresh frames, 10 val drives, 60 sim episodes

notes.title: A rank-8 vision adapter puts lane lines within 3 to 5 cm of road paint and keeps push recovery when drives are balanced
notes.summary: Trained on 4 dual-camera visor-mount drives with comma's policy frozen and merged back into an ordinary ONNX file, a rank-8 low-rank adapter on N16's vision weights moved full-sequence validation lane-line error across all 10 unseen drives (60,787 steps, 4,552 paint frames) from 0.196 / 0.254 m (1.45 m warp) and 0.488 / 0.505 m (exact geometry) to 0.032 / 0.032 m (0.023 / 0.026 m on 2 locked hold-out drives, and 0.057 / 0.040 m unchanged on f22e06e5_56320). On the same 87 dense closed-loop windows (435 episodes per policy), the balanced 1.45 m adapter reached 71.6 to 72.4 % relative push recovery (+2.3 to +3.2 points over the 1.45 m baseline by window, 10-drive CIs touching or straddling zero; +4.6 to +5.5 points over a -0.239 m camera warp while holding within 0.005 to 0.021 m of centre); a 3-arm single-seed ablation showed uncapping an 88-minute highway drive (84.5 % of trainable steps and 3.7x total updates) cost 7.5 points of push recovery and adding open-loop turn supervision on the uncapped corpus cost a further 2.0 points.
notes.grade: Measured offline across all 60,787 5 Hz steps of 10 validation drives, 2 locked hold-out drives, the untouched 2026-11-10 road-paint script (1,384 to 1,529 frames per model), and 87 paired closed-loop windows; nothing deployed to the truck.
notes.result: lane error 0.032 / 0.032 m; 71.6 to 72.4 % rel. recovery

notes.title: N16 puts each lane line about 0.23 m too close to the camera on the truck
notes.summary: Against paint measured in the camera's own frames on the road plane, each of N16's inner lane lines is 0.21 m (highway, 34 and 42 frames) to 0.26 m (town, 102 frames) farther out than N16 puts it, the same at every distance from the camera from 0.55 to 2.15 m. A fixed outward move fitted on one road type leaves 0.03 to 0.06 m on the other; one scale leaves up to 0.18 m. The tablet's 3D scene now moves the lines out by 0.23 m and onto the truck's centreline; on 9 of 10 checked moments it draws them within 0.10 m of the paint, where before the right line was 0.41 to 0.51 m too close.
notes.grade: Measured on recorded G55 drives from the current camera mount: 178 straight-road frames from four drives, highway and town, by day. Inner lane lines only; road edges, curves and night not measured.
notes.result: each lane line 0.21 to 0.26 m outward of N16's

notes.title: The simulator could not draw highway views: one source frame every 0.2 s was too few
notes.summary: In the closed-loop simulator, 35 of 95 windows at 30 to 33 m/s and 18 of 24 at 33 to 36 m/s ended the unpushed episode in a view it could not draw, and none between 12 and 24 m/s. The view is warped from a recorded frame kept every 0.2 s, up to 6.6 m behind the truck at 33 m/s; warped past about 6 m the near road is left empty. Drawing from every recorded frame cut such endings from 61 of 160 unpushed episodes to 1 on the same 80 windows. They had been scored as the model failing to recover.
notes.grade: Measured in simulation on recorded G55 drives from after the camera re-aim: 320 windows for the speed table, 2,880 warps of real frames on 80 windows for coverage, 80 windows for the before and after. A correction to the method; the model comparison it interrupted is not finished.
notes.result: undrawn unpushed episodes 61 of 160, then 1 of 160

notes.title: comma's 2026-11-05 model recovers more pushes than N16 in the simulator
notes.summary: Untrained, comma's f22e06e5_56320 recovered 49.3 to 69.5 % of pushed episodes on 73 validation windows from 9 drives, against 40.8 to 58.6 % for N16 (+7.2 to +11.0 points; the doublet interval includes zero). At three times the residual scale its gain over N16 at 3x was +4.8 to +8.2 points, every validation interval including zero. Unpushed, it ends 0.07 to 0.16 m right of the driver's path.
notes.grade: Measured in simulation on recorded G55 drives, 9 validation and 2 hold-out drives, all from before the camera re-aim; untrained, no bar set in advance, nothing deployed.
notes.result: +7.2 to +11.0 points over N16 as shipped

notes.title: Imitation training of N16's residual head did not beat its untrained start
notes.summary: Trained in the simulator to copy an oracle's steering on the states it visits (DAgger), N16's residual head recovered more pushes on its two training drives but did not beat the untrained 3x start on 9 validation and 2 hold-out drives. There its unpushed line sat 0.14 to 0.37 m left of the driver's path; a follow-up check ties that shift to the camera being re-aimed between the training and the evaluation drives.
notes.grade: Measured in simulation on recorded G55 drives: 2 training, 9 validation and 2 hold-out drives, and a check on 3 locked-test drives with nothing claimed; a negative result, nothing deployed.
notes.result: -17.5 to +7.9 points against the 3x start

notes.title: N16's residual head at two to four times its scale recovers more pushes
notes.summary: Untrained, N16 with comma's residual steering head at three times its shipped scale recovered 52.7 to 68.5 % of pushed episodes on 73 validation windows from 9 drives, against 40.8 to 58.6 % as shipped (+7.9 to +27.7 points, every 95 % interval over drives above zero). Most of the gain is fewer episodes leaving the area the simulator can draw. Corrected 2026-11-09: the first slow-drift run pushed 1.6 times the stated distance; its figures here are from a rerun.
notes.grade: Measured in simulation on recorded G55 drives, 9 validation and 2 hold-out drives; untrained, locked test not run, nothing deployed (the truck runs scale 1).
notes.result: +7.9 to +27.7 points recovered at 3x

notes.title: A trained steering correction on N16 recovers more often in simulation
notes.summary: On 44 held-out simulator windows, a TD3-trained correction on N16 recovered from 1.5 m pushes 0.76 of the time against 0.58 for its untrained starting point (+0.18 [+0.13, +0.33]). Against the driver's recorded line the gain was +0.07 at 1.5 m and +0.01 at 1.0 m.
notes.grade: Measured in simulation on recorded G55 drives, 3 held-out drives; exploratory, locked test not run, nothing deployed.

notes.title: Camera position moves where N16 holds the truck in its lane
notes.summary: In simulation, moving N16's virtual camera sideways moves its held lane position by -0.97 m per metre of shift. A road-plane warp for a lens 0.239 m right of centre took back about half of the +0.191 m median shift in the hold and restored 0.394 of 1.0 m pushes against 0.197 uncorrected (base 0.509).
notes.grade: Measured in simulation on recorded G55 drives (135 dev day windows, mirror-mount windows emulating the visor mount); not tested on a real drive.
notes.result: -0.97 m per m of camera shift

notes.title: N16's frozen vision tokens do not replace a box detector
notes.summary: A head on N16's frozen vision tokens found 2.7 % of vehicles at IoU 0.5, against 55.5 % for YOLO26s on the same frames. Added to the box, the tokens gave a speed error of 3.88 to 4.44 m/s against 2.31 m/s for the analytical tracker.
notes.grade: Measured offline on recorded G55 drives with hand-checked and hindsight truth; exploratory, one head configuration, nothing deployed.
notes.result: 2.7 % of vehicles, against 55.5 % for YOLO26s

notes.title: The camera loop ran below 20 Hz because OpenBLAS threads spun
notes.summary: On N16 drives the camera loop ran 17.7 to 18.8 Hz: a serial decoder skipped ticks while OpenBLAS worker threads used 1.75 cores. With one OpenBLAS thread per service, three drives held 19.91 to 19.92 Hz.
notes.grade: Measured on recorded drives, in replay on the truck's Jetson board, and on three drives after the fix was installed.

notes.title: comma's models turn the wrong way first because of the base policy
notes.summary: In 258 of 258 pushes where a full comma model first steered with the push, its residual-off copy did too. The residual removes 61-88% of these turns but sits at its 1.0 m/s² bound on the rest.
notes.grade: Measured in simulation on recorded G55 drives with comma's own residual-off files; exploratory, one seed, daytime reprojection only, not a deployed change.

notes.title: After a push, N16 still encodes the truck's offset and heading
notes.summary: A linear probe reads the truck's lateral offset from N16's vision tokens at R² 0.84-0.93 and from its base summary at 0.87-0.98 on held-out sessions. The wrong-way first turn comes from the base's readout of yaw rate, not from missing information.
notes.grade: Measured in open-loop simulation on recorded G55 drives; exploratory, daytime stock-lens windows and N16 only, not a deployed change.
notes.result: R² 0.84-0.93 from the tokens

notes.title: Teaching comma's world model to keep a sideways offset
notes.summary: By day comma's world model as shipped already puts the road at a commanded offset (road gain 1.05 at 3 s). Fine-tuning made it overshoot (1.24), reward training did not pass its gate, and no version holds the road at night.
notes.grade: Measured in simulation on recorded G55 drives; exploratory, small test sets, not a deployed change.
notes.result: road gain 1.05 at 3 s; fine-tuned 1.24

notes.title: A truck model learned from the G55's CAN predicts motion better
notes.summary: On 12 held-out drives a recurrent network learned from the truck's CAN data has a sideways error of 0.29 m after 4 s of free running, against 7.34 m for the hand-built model and 0.66 m for the same equations refit. It fails a stopping check, so the simulator's default stays hand-built.
notes.grade: Measured on recorded G55 drives, with the test set scored once per candidate; exploratory, one truck configuration, no steering actuator.
notes.result: 0.29 m after 4 s, against 7.34 m
